claims.text: Adding the entry breaks the behavior registry gate unless two lockstep edits land with it: one hooks/behavior-dispositions.tsv row of disposition registry naming the entry (else 'active behavior has no registry disposition'), and that inventory id in EXPECTED_INVENTORY_IDS (else 'inventory set mismatch'); with both, validation passes.

The behavior registry gate is reached only through hooks/plugin-source-gates.sh (GATES at :97): at commit by the installed precommit-gates.sh when plugin.json names afk, and in pull-request CI by the target branch's runner and the branch's own; no plugin gate runs at Stop, where both hooks files run only 'repo-list Stop' and this repository's .afk/hooks.json declares nothing.

The entry's doctrine 'DELEGATION.md §Spawn rules' resolves to the heading at DELEGATION.md:22; the validator also requires its body to carry '${AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT}/DELEGATION.md' (it is not self-contained) and refuses claude, codex, chatgpt, gemini or cursor in the body; a simulated 2-line body with that pointer validates, and the same body naming a harness is refused.

Two more gates read the new body without naming the registry: native-contract check A scans every plugin *.md outside the provider homes and docs/afk/, BEHAVIORS.md included, for harness words, and the genericity gate scans the added lines of every changed plugin .md for ticket-shaped ids and product symbols.

The SessionStart drift handler hooks/behavior-drift.sh, registered in both hooks files, audits only the session's own target and prints one '/afk:setup' line on drift, never a body; the audit compares the whole installed block with a fresh render, so after the change every block rendered before it reads stale until setup renders again, while registry-revision stays 3.

Setup row H7 renders the active plugin's registry once per enabled provider against that provider's own root and installs it with install_block.py; render validates the registry against that root's doctrine files, so a provider root whose DELEGATION.md lacks the 'Spawn rules' heading fails the render and the recipe exits 1 for every remaining target; install_block.py itself checks no size or content and is not edited.
